## T9 regulatory reading (main text)

**Why.** The six seed-fixed figures in the harvest come from perasset_v2_results.json, which is the 140-name panel, so writing them into a 200-name note would recreate the mismatch. The table's EVT row (frtb battery pipeline, breach 0.88%) and the FZ0 accuracy layer (breach 1.02%) are different implementations, so the sentence names each: the table row's per-asset Kupiec pass rate (86%, frtb_table_200) and the accuracy layer's battery figures (exception_battery_results.json, canon200: Kupiec 83.5%, Christoffersen 89%, 97.5% 73% and 77.5%, date-clustered t 0.29 and 1.60, body t 4.11 and 4.43).

**Before.**

```
date-clustered restatement (Online Appendix Figure~OA.2): per asset the
EVT-tailed residual-hybrid passes Kupiec at 99\% for $82\%$ of names and
Christoffersen conditional coverage for $89\%$ (at 97.5\%, $71\%$ and $79\%$), and the date-clustered test passes at 99\% ($t=0.93$) and marginally at 97.5\% ($t=1.85$) while the raw residual-hybrid is rejected ($t=4.2$):
```

**After.**

```
date-clustered restatement: per asset the EVT-tailed residual-hybrid of this
table passes Kupiec at 99\% for $86\%$ of names (Online Appendix Figure~OA.2), and the accuracy layer of the
FZ0 comparison passes Kupiec for $84\%$ and Christoffersen conditional coverage for $89\%$ (at 97.5\%, $73\%$ and $78\%$), with the date-clustered test passing at 99\% ($t=0.29$) and at 97.5\% ($t=1.60$) while its pooled body without the EVT tail is rejected ($t=4.1$ and $4.4$):
```

## D1 Beta-t-EGARCH in the decomposition (main text)

**Why.** The R56 harvest's first text consequence. bench_all_bteg_results.json, pinball: param_bteg vs GARCH-t +3.561 (DM 8.8) top decile, +0.74 (9.37) overall; engine vs param_bteg -1.157 (-4.69) top, -0.481 (-5.09) overall, -0.398 (-4.15) deciles 1-9; engine_bteg vs param_bteg +0.272 (2.04) top, -0.052 (-0.88) overall, -0.092 (-1.51) deciles 1-9. A plain Beta-t-EGARCH beats the GARCH-t-scaled estimator on pinball everywhere under frozen fits; stating it here is the honest form of the decomposition.

**Before.**

```
diagnostic of shape alone.
```

**After.**

```
diagnostic of shape alone. A Beta-$t$-EGARCH fitted by maximum likelihood \citep{harvey2013dynamic}, whose score-driven update bounds the response to a large residual, makes the same point without a cap to choose. Under the frozen fits it beats GARCH-$t$ by $+3.56\%$ (DM 8.8) in the top decile and $+0.74\%$ (DM 9.4) overall, and it beats the estimator on the GARCH-$t$ scale in every region ($+1.16\%$, DM 4.7, in the top decile; $+0.48\%$, DM 5.1, overall). With the estimator rebuilt on the Beta-$t$-EGARCH scale, the flexible tail's edge over that model's own Student-$t$ tail is $+0.27\%$ (DM 2.0) in the top decile and within noise elsewhere, so on a robust scale the frontier is flat.
```

## Not in R58, needs a decision or a run

1. **Stage 4 (conformal overlay).** The R54 harvest found the shift is estimated against the body and applied to the engine, double counting the EVT branch. On the 200-name panel two Stage-4 sentences also become false: 'This distribution-free layer repairs the 97.5% level that each model in the comparison set otherwise fails' and 'the conformal stage is the only reason any entrant passes Kupiec at 97.5%', because rolling FHS passes pooled Kupiec at 97.5% (p = 0.91). Options: drop the overlay from the paper, or keep it as a disclosed variant with the double counting stated and those two sentences rewritten. The mixed-run overlay figures (1.66/1.63%, DM -1.8/-2.01, 48/47%, 71/72%) go with whichever is chosen.
2. **Cold start.** The R54 harvest: own 20-day vol carrying the pooled shape beats every peer-scale configuration from day 6 by 10-13%; days 1-5 breach 7.13% at 1%; the flexible learner on day-one peer features loses to pooled empirical quantiles at every age. The paper's 6-10% first-month edge over own history has not been run against own_short_pool. Run that head-to-head before Section 6 is rewritten.
3. **Score invariance** (indicator agreement 0.985-0.993 across three filters): one sentence for the score-use paragraph, optional.
